title: Getting started with FishDiveR
text: unit analysis day: 24-hour period, midnight midnight local time, becomes one row data cluster. Wavelet analysis. continuous wavelet transform finds strongly depth record oscillates period (example every 20 minutes, every 3 hours, day) every point time. Unlike Fourier transform, copes behaviour changes record. Daily statistics. wavelet results summarised day period (mean power, power variance, mean amplitude ). Separately, daily depth statistics calculated depth record : mean maximum depth, vertical speed, time near surface , optionally, differences day night. Principal component analysis (PCA). Neighbouring wavelet periods carry similar information, many wavelet statistics condensed principal components. K-means clustering. principal components depth statistics combined, days grouped k clusters similar behaviour. method described detail Beale et al. (2026), Movement Ecology 14:8, https://doi.org/10.1186/s40462-025-00622-w.

text: import_tag_data() reads csv archive date-time column depth column, crops deployment, whole days (midnight midnight) local time zone. cropped record saved archive_days.rds tag’s folder. things check data: Time zone. Days split local midnight, give time zone animal . Time zones daylight saving supported, clock changes create days 23 25 hours. Date-time format. title: Getting started with FishDiveR
text: create_wavelet() runs continuous wavelet transform range periods, lower_period_mins upper_period_hours, suboctaves periods doubling period. Lower period. shortest cycle analysed. 5 minutes captures short dives, sampling interval allows; must least twice sampling interval. example uses 30 minutes keep vignette quick. Upper period. longest cycle analysed. 24 hours focuses daily behaviour. Sub-octaves. 12 gives periods include 24, 12 6 hours exactly, 12 periods . Use settings tags cluster together. plot_wavelet = TRUE, power spectrum saved tag’s 2_Wavelet_Figures folder. Red shows strong oscillation period time.  Wavelets long, high-frequency records can need lot memory: year 1-second sampling can need tens gigabytes. vignette("large-records", package = "FishDiveR") explains estimate reduce thin_archive().
code: wavelet <- create_wavelet(   archive = archive_days,   tag_ID = "data",   lower_period_mins = 30,   upper_period_hours = 24,   suboctaves = 12,   output = TRUE,   output_folder = project,   plot_wavelet = TRUE,   interactive_mode = FALSE )

title: Getting started with FishDiveR
text: create_wavelet_stats() summarises wavelet day period: mean variance amplitude, phase power, mean squared power. create_depth_stats() calculates daily statistics full-resolution depth record: mean, standard deviation, minimum maximum depth, mean vertical speed, maximum descent ascent speeds, skewness kurtosis depth, proportion time near surface. diel = TRUE adds differences night day statistics, standardised day’s maximum depth. Sunrise sunset come GPS file daily positions (columns date, lat lon), fixed sunrise_time sunset_time.
code: wave_stats <- create_wavelet_stats(wavelet, tag_ID = "data", output = TRUE, output_folder = project) dim(wave_stats) #> [1]  10 478 depth_stats <- create_depth_stats(   archive = archive_days,   tag_ID = "data",   diel = TRUE,   GPS = file.path(example_folder, "data", "GPS.csv"),   sunset_type = "civil",   output = TRUE,   output_folder = project ) names(depth_stats) #>  [1] "date_only"          "depth.mean"         "depth.sd"           #>  [4] "depth.min"          "depth.max"          "mean.abs_vv"        #>  [7] "max.dsc_vv"         "max.asc_vv"         "skewness_depth"     #> [10] "kurtosis_depth"     "surface_proportion" "st_mean_diff"       #> [13] "st_sd_diff"         "st_range_diff"      "st_absVV_diff"      #> [16] "st_dscVV_diff"      "st_ascVV_diff"      "surf_prop_diff"

title: Getting started with FishDiveR
text: pca_data() collects chosen wavelet statistics tags analyse. Mean power, power variance mean amplitude defaults: capture variance fewest principal components. choosing many components keep, look eigenvalues cumulative variance explain. Asking 50 components returns eigenvalues. Common choices components eigenvalues 1 , enough components explain least 70% variance. three components explain 90%. combine_data() joins day’s principal component scores depth statistics, ready clustering.
code: pc_data <- pca_data(   tag_vector = "data",   data_folder = project,   power_mean = TRUE,   power_variance = TRUE,   amplitude_mean = TRUE ) all_pcs <- pca_results(pc_data, No_pcs = 50, plot_eigenvalues = FALSE, interactive_mode = FALSE) round(head(all_pcs$eig, 8), 2) #>        eigenvalue percentage of variance cumulative percentage of variance #> comp 1     108.02                  52.95                             52.95 #> comp 2      55.82                  27.36                             80.31 #> comp 3      24.25                  11.89                             92.20 #> comp 4       8.77                   4.30                             96.50 #> comp 5       3.95                   1.94                             98.43 #> comp 6       1.80                   0.88                             99.32 #> comp 7       0.87                   0.43                             99.74 #> comp 8       0.32                   0.16                             99.90 pc_results <- pca_results(pc_data, No_pcs = 3, plot_eigenvalues = FALSE, interactive_mode = FALSE) pc_scores <- pca_scores(pc_results, plot_loadings = FALSE) kmeans_data <- combine_data(tag_vector = "data", data_folder = project, pc_scores = pc_scores) dim(kmeans_data) #> [1] 10 22

what: 5. Choose the number of clusters and cluster the days
title: Getting started with FishDiveR
text: select_k() runs k-means number clusters Max.k, plots within-cluster sum squares (, “elbow” plot) mean silhouette width (B). Look number near elbow, clusters stop reducing sum squares much, silhouette width high. K-means starts random cluster centres, set seed reproducible results.  k_clustering() assigns day one k clusters. output = TRUE also saves 3D plot first three principal components figures cluster’s mean variable values. ten days, clusters just illustration: real analyses need many days meaningful clusters.
code: set.seed(123) select_k(kmeans_data, Max.k = 8, v_line = 4) set.seed(123) kmeans_result <- k_clustering(kmeans_data, k = 4, nstart = 50, output = FALSE) table(Cluster = kmeans_result$cluster) #> Cluster #> 1 2 3 4  #> 2 1 2 5

title: Thin a depth record to a longer sampling interval — thin_archive
text: block interval_s seconds becomes one record, timed start block, mean depth (mean temperature, present) block. Averaging, rather keeping every nth record, stops movements faster new interval appearing false longer cycles (aliasing). Thinning removes cycles shorter twice new interval. rule thumb, keep least 20 records per cycle wavelet's lower period, .e. interval_s <= lower_period_mins * 60 / 20: 15 seconds 5 minute lower period. Keep using full record create_depth_stats(), averaging slightly reduces maximum depths. Tags clustered together thinned interval.
